candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is 'Topical corticosteroid withdrawal,' which encompasses the full syndrome triggered by abrupt cessation of prolonged potent topical steroid use. Perioral dermatitis can be a component or manifestation of this syndrome, but C001 names only one phenotypic subtype and does not capture the withdrawal mechanism or the broader diagnostic entity. Additionally, the dominant findings are periorbital pustular plaques, not the typical perioral distribution, making even this subtype label imprecise.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Perioral dermatitis is a recognized manifestation/complication of prolonged topical corticosteroid use and can occur during withdrawal, but it is a specific clinical phenotype rather than the overarching diagnosis of topical corticosteroid withdrawal itself; the case also features predominantly periorbital (not perioral) distribution with 'lakes of pus,' more consistent with the steroid rosacea/withdrawal flare pattern than classic perioral dermatitis

case_quality_flags: Classic topical corticosteroid withdrawal (steroid-induced rosacea/red skin syndrome) with abrupt cessation after 2 years of potent facial triamcinolone; periorbital predominance with pustular lakes is characteristic
Initial misdiagnosis as eczema herpeticum and acyclovir prescription noted — relevant to differential but does not alter reference diagnosis
